title: Triangles: Congruence of Triangles
seo_title: Triangles Class 9 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 7)
standard_text: Congruence of triangles: SAS (motivate after illustrating), ASA, SSS and RHS congruence; the angles opposite equal sides of a triangle are equal, and the sides opposite equal angles are equal (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 9 Triangles worksheet (NCERT Chapter 7): congruence criteria SAS, ASA, AAS, SSS and RHS, CPCT, isosceles triangle properties and algebra. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: AAA and SSA do not prove congruence. Then use CPCT.
body_html:
How it works

Two triangles are congruent if their corresponding sides and angles are equal. Write the vertices in matching order: △ABC ≅ △PQR means A ↔ P, B ↔ Q, C ↔ R.

Criteria: SAS (two sides and the included angle), ASA, AAS, SSS and RHS (right angle, hypotenuse, one side). AAA and SSA do not prove congruence.

Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are equal (CPCT). In an isosceles triangle the angles opposite the equal sides are equal.

Example

AB = PQ, ∠B = ∠Q, BC = QR. Are △ABC and △PQR congruent?

Two sides and the included angle

Answer: Yes, by SAS

Example

In △ABC, AB = AC and ∠B = 50°. Find ∠A.

∠C = 50°

180° − 100°

Answer: 80°

Common mistakes

  • Using SAS when the angle is not between the two sides (SSA).
  • Thinking three equal angles (AAA) prove congruence. They only give the same shape.
  • Matching the vertices out of order when writing △ABC ≅ △PQR.

faq.q: What are the criteria for congruence of triangles?
faq.a: SAS, ASA, AAS, SSS and RHS (for right triangles: right angle, hypotenuse and one side).
Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are equal. Once two triangles are proved congruent, their matching sides and angles are equal.

faq.q: Why is SSA not a congruence criterion?
faq.a: Two sides and an angle that is not between them can make two different triangles, so they do not fix the triangle.

faq.q: What is special about an isosceles triangle?
faq.a: The angles opposite its equal sides are equal, and conversely, sides opposite equal angles are equal.

items.q: Given △WCS ≅ △PRF, which segment is congruent to SC?
items.e: Match the letters in order: S → F and C → R. So SC ≅ FR.

items.q: Given △PWT ≅ △CLM, which angle is congruent to ∠T?
items.e: T is in the same position as M in the statement, so ∠T ≅ ∠M.

items.q: Given △GNA ≅ △QMD, which segment is congruent to AN?
items.e: Match the letters in order: A → D and N → M. So AN ≅ DM.

items.q: Given △HYX ≅ △BJK, which segment is congruent to YX?
items.e: Match the letters in order: Y → J and X → K. So YX ≅ JK.

items.q: Given △PUK ≅ △CGF, which angle is congruent to ∠P?
items.e: P is in the same position as C in the statement, so ∠P ≅ ∠C.

items.q: Given △ABS ≅ △DWM, which segment is congruent to SB?
items.e: Match the letters in order: S → M and B → W. So SB ≅ MW.

items.q: Given △ZVH ≅ △UAC, complete the statement: △ZHV ≅ ?
items.e: Keep each pair of matching vertices together: Z ↔ U, H ↔ C, V ↔ A. So △ZHV ≅ △UCA.

items.q: Given △GJV ≅ △FHD, complete the statement: △GVJ ≅ ?
items.e: Keep each pair of matching vertices together: G ↔ F, V ↔ D, J ↔ H. So △GVJ ≅ △FDH.

items.q: Given △KDN ≅ △VMT, complete the statement: △DNK ≅ ?
items.e: Keep each pair of matching vertices together: D ↔ M, N ↔ T, K ↔ V. So △DNK ≅ △MTV.

items.q: Given △ZNF ≅ △GVU, which segment is congruent to NF?
items.e: Match the letters in order: N → V and F → U. So NF ≅ VU.

items.q: Given △SXU ≅ △TAM, which angle is congruent to ∠S?
items.e: S is in the same position as T in the statement, so ∠S ≅ ∠T.

items.q: Given △UCL ≅ △YHP, which angle is congruent to ∠U?
items.e: U is in the same position as Y in the statement, so ∠U ≅ ∠Y.

items.q: Given △JTM ≅ △ZKR, which segment is congruent to MT?
items.e: Match the letters in order: M → R and T → K. So MT ≅ RK.

items.q: Given △ZCJ ≅ △SKT, which angle is congruent to ∠C?
items.e: C is in the same position as K in the statement, so ∠C ≅ ∠K.

items.q: Given △KER ≅ △HPU, which segment is congruent to ER?
items.e: Match the letters in order: E → P and R → U. So ER ≅ PU.

items.q: Given △RXQ ≅ △EAN, which angle is congruent to ∠Q?
items.e: Q is in the same position as N in the statement, so ∠Q ≅ ∠N.

items.q: Given △YTR ≅ △PUE, which segment is congruent to RT?
items.e: Match the letters in order: R → E and T → U. So RT ≅ EU.

items.q: Given △HXY ≅ △RLD, which angle is congruent to ∠Y?
items.e: Y is in the same position as D in the statement, so ∠Y ≅ ∠D.

items.q: Given △WSF ≅ △RJQ, which angle is congruent to ∠W?
items.e: W is in the same position as R in the statement, so ∠W ≅ ∠R.

items.q: Given △RCV ≅ △UBL, which angle is congruent to ∠R?
items.e: R is in the same position as U in the statement, so ∠R ≅ ∠U.

items.q: In △RST and △UVW, ∠R ≅ ∠U and ∠S ≅ ∠V. What else do you need to prove △RST ≅ △UVW by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. RS is between ∠R and ∠S: RS ≅ UV.

items.q: In △JKL and △MNO, ∠J ≅ ∠M and ∠K ≅ ∠N. What else do you need to prove △JKL ≅ △MNO by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. JK is between ∠J and ∠K: JK ≅ MN.

items.q: In △JKL and △MNO, ∠J ≅ ∠M and ∠K ≅ ∠N. What else do you need to prove △JKL ≅ △MNO by AAS?
items.e: AAS needs a side that is not between the two angles, such as KL: KL ≅ NO.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, ∠A ≅ ∠D and ∠B ≅ ∠E. What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. AB is between ∠A and ∠B: AB ≅ DE.

items.q: In △JKL and △MNO, JK ≅ MN and KL ≅ NO. What else do you need to prove △JKL ≅ △MNO by SSS?
items.e: SSS needs the third pair of sides: JL ≅ MO.

items.q: In △GHI and △LMN, GH ≅ LM and ∠H ≅ ∠M. What else do you need to prove △GHI ≅ △LMN by SAS?
items.e: SAS needs the angle between the two sides. ∠H is between GH and HI: HI ≅ MN.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, ∠P ≅ ∠X and ∠Q ≅ ∠Y. What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. PQ is between ∠P and ∠Q: PQ ≅ XY.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, ∠R and ∠Z are right angles, and PQ ≅ XY (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by RHS?
items.e: RHS needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. PR and XZ are legs: PR ≅ XZ.

items.q: In △GHI and △LMN, GH ≅ LM and HI ≅ MN. What else do you need to prove △GHI ≅ △LMN by SSS?
items.e: SSS needs the third pair of sides: GI ≅ LN.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, AB ≅ DE and BC ≅ EF. What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by SSS?
items.e: SSS needs the third pair of sides: AC ≅ DF.

items.q: In △GHI and △LMN, ∠I and ∠N are right angles, and GH ≅ LM (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △GHI ≅ △LMN by RHS?
items.e: RHS needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. GI and LN are legs: GI ≅ LN.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, PQ ≅ XY and ∠Q ≅ ∠Y. What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by SAS?
items.e: SAS needs the angle between the two sides. ∠Q is between PQ and QR: QR ≅ YZ.

items.q: In △JKL and △MNO, JK ≅ MN and ∠K ≅ ∠N. What else do you need to prove △JKL ≅ △MNO by SAS?
items.e: SAS needs the angle between the two sides. ∠K is between JK and KL: KL ≅ NO.

items.q: In △RST and △UVW, ∠T and ∠W are right angles, and RS ≅ UV (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △RST ≅ △UVW by RHS?
items.e: RHS needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. RT and UW are legs: RT ≅ UW.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, AB ≅ DE and ∠B ≅ ∠E. What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by SAS?
items.e: SAS needs the angle between the two sides. ∠B is between AB and BC: BC ≅ EF.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, ∠A ≅ ∠D and ∠B ≅ ∠E. What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by AAS?
items.e: AAS needs a side that is not between the two angles, such as BC: BC ≅ EF.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, PQ ≅ XY and QR ≅ YZ. What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by SSS?
items.e: SSS needs the third pair of sides: PR ≅ XZ.

items.q: In △JKL and △MNO, ∠L and ∠O are right angles, and JK ≅ MN (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △JKL ≅ △MNO by RHS?
items.e: RHS needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. JL and MO are legs: JL ≅ MO.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, ∠C and ∠F are right angles, and AB ≅ DE (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by RHS?
items.e: RHS needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. AC and DF are legs: AC ≅ DF.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, ∠P ≅ ∠X and ∠Q ≅ ∠Y. What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by AAS?
items.e: AAS needs a side that is not between the two angles, such as QR: QR ≅ YZ.

items.q: In △PQR, PQ = PR and ∠Q = 50°. Find ∠P.
items.e: ∠R = ∠Q = 50° (opposite equal sides). ∠P = 180° − 2 × 50° = 80°.

items.q: In △PQR, PQ = PR and ∠Q = 20°. Find ∠P.
items.e: ∠R = ∠Q = 20° (opposite equal sides). ∠P = 180° − 2 × 20° = 140°.

items.q: In △XYZ, XY = XZ. Which two angles are equal?
items.e: The equal angles are opposite the equal sides XZ and XY. ∠Y and ∠Z.

items.q: In △PQR, PQ = PR and ∠Q = 73°. Find ∠P.
items.e: ∠R = ∠Q = 73° (opposite equal sides). ∠P = 180° − 2 × 73° = 34°.

In △PQR, PQ = PR and ∠Q = 33°. Find ∠P.

items.q: In △ABC, AB = AC and ∠A = 112°. Find ∠B.
items.e: Angles opposite equal sides are equal, so ∠B = ∠C = (180° − 112°) ÷ 2 = 34°.

items.q: In △ABC, ∠B = ∠C. Which two sides are equal?
items.e: The sides opposite the equal angles B and C are AC and AB. AB and AC.
